title: Automatic cross-region promotion of the MySQL primary

source.note: Adapted from GitHub's October 21, 2018 post-incident analysis (Orchestrator promoted a primary in another region after a 43 s partition).

input.objective: Reduce MySQL primary-failure recovery time for the main application from ~30 minutes of manual work to under one minute.
constraints: The product must keep accepting writes during a single-host failure.
Budget allows the current two-region footprint, nothing more.
input.context: Main app (Rails monolith) runs in region East; its MySQL clusters have a primary in East plus replicas in East and in region West (~60 ms RTT) for disaster recovery. Asynchronous replication. Application servers only run in East. Failovers are currently done by on-call engineers following a runbook. Orchestrator (topology manager) is already deployed with Raft consensus across East, West and a third public-cloud site, and discovers the full topology.
input.proposed_solution: Enable Orchestrator automated recovery for all clusters: when the primary is unreachable for 30 seconds, Orchestrator (with Raft quorum across the three sites, so a single site cannot decide alone) promotes the most up-to-date replica regardless of region, repoints the other replicas and updates service discovery so applications follow the new primary automatically. Pseudo-GTID is enabled, so no binlog position bookkeeping is needed. We will test it with game days that kill primary hosts in East.
input.environment: MySQL 5.7, Orchestrator 3.x with Raft, Consul for service discovery, semi-synchronous replication not enabled.

ground_truth.material_issue: A transient network partition between East and the other sites makes the quorum promote a West replica: writes already accepted in East but not yet replicated are stranded (split data), and the East-only application now writes across ~60 ms RTT to West, degrading every request. Promotion must be region-constrained (or require the app tier to move with it) and must account for unreplicated writes; partition-only events should not trigger cross-region promotion.
required_observations: A network partition (not a host failure) can trigger promotion in the other region
Writes accepted in East but not replicated are lost/diverged after promotion (async replication)
Applications stay in East and would write cross-region with high latency
Restrict automatic promotion to the same region / require explicit decision for cross-region
